title: How to Use Both Halves of AC Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav pedals to college with both legs pushing, one after the other. A half-wave rectifier is like a one-legged rider: it throws away half of every wave. How do we use both halves?

On live breadboards we build the centre-tap full-wave rectifier (two diodes taking turns) and the bridge rectifier (four diodes in a diamond, two working at a time), with the oscilloscope showing the input (CH1) and the output (CH2) and electrons crossing the load the same way in both halves. We derive V_dc = 2V_m/π (about 0.637 V_m, double the half-wave value), then compare centre tap and bridge: output frequency 2f, peak inverse voltage 2V_m vs V_m, diodes, centre tap, diode drops and the 81.2% maximum efficiency. A worked example, the exam trap (centre-tap PIV is 2V_m), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 43 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits | ISC Class 12 Physics: Semiconductor Electronics (diode as a rectifier).
